what_happened: The operator ran CI routing item 5 (job 3htd) directly, right after item 4 landed (#125). They did not wait for Athena's plan to reach it. The reason given was that CI routing is the owner's speed priority and the plan still does not put it first. This is the fifth time the operator has overridden the plan's order for the speed work.
cause: The plan still takes no input from the owner's stated priority and has no way to keep a multi-item series together. Rungs are ordered by default type and position, so each later item in a priority series (CI routing items 4, 5 and so on) falls back to its default place. Nothing compares the plan's order with the owner's latest priority. The queue has no priority support either, so the operator's only lever is to bypass the plan. Four earlier cases and the gaps logged from them were never turned into a scheduled fix, so each new item in the series repeats the bypass.
prevention: Make the owner's priority a recorded input to planning, and have the queue honor it. The owner states an ordered priority list, or marks a series such as CI routing as top priority. The plan sorts by that list before default rung type. When one item of a priority series lands, the next item is queued ahead of non-priority work automatically. A check flags any plan whose order contradicts the recorded priority, and fails planning until fixed. The queue also needs a priority field, so no operator bypass is needed.
proposed_request: Make Athena's planning follow the owner's stated priority, so the operator never has to run priority work out of order. Outcome: (1) The owner's priority list, including multi-item series such as the CI routing items, is stored in a repo file that planning reads. (2) The plan orders rungs by that priority before default work type, and when one item in a priority series lands, the next item in the series is placed first in the plan. (3) The queue supports a priority value, so priority items are drained before others without killing a running job. (4) A check fails plan generation if the plan order contradicts the recorded priority. Acceptance: a test with a plan containing CI routing items 5 and later, plus 10 unrelated rungs, shows the CI routing items scheduled first. A second test shows the drain picks a priority item ahead of older non-priority items.
